description: Fix the CAM-178 uid/gid re-home block in .devcontainer/Dockerfile so the cam-worker image builds on a macOS host where HOST_GID=20 collides with the base image group.

officialDocsConsulted.summary: Confirmed the invariant the fix depends on: usermod -g/--gid GROUP requires that 'The group must exist.', so usermod -g HOST_GID cannot run unconditionally when no group owns that gid (hence the getent branch is mandatory). groupmod -n only renames a group; it does not free the gid, which is the exact CAM-178 build failure.

userStories.title: Rewrite re-home block with getent gid-collision branch
userStories.description: As a cam operator on macOS (host gid=20 collides with the oven/bun:1.2-slim base gid-20 group), I need the .devcontainer/Dockerfile re-home RUN block to branch on whether the host gid already exists so the cam-worker image builds successfully and the bun user ends at HOST_UID:HOST_GID with /workspace writable, instead of failing at build time with 'groupmod: GID 20 already exists'.
acceptanceCriteria: The re-home RUN block in .devcontainer/Dockerfile contains no `groupmod -n` and no `_rehomed` group-name rename; the rename-based collision guard is gone. [oracle: file-assert ! grep -qE 'groupmod -n|_rehomed' .devcontainer/Dockerfile]

The re-home block branches on `getent group "$HOST_GID"`: when the group exists it runs `usermod -u "$HOST_UID" -g "$HOST_GID" bun`; when it does not it runs `groupmod -g "$HOST_GID" bun` then `usermod -u "$HOST_UID" bun`. [oracle: file-assert grep -q 'getent group "$HOST_GID"' .devcontainer/Dockerfile && grep -q 'usermod -u "$HOST_UID" -g "$HOST_GID" bun' .devcontainer/Dockerfile]
The block still ends with `chown -R "$HOST_UID:$HOST_GID" /home/bun`. [oracle: file-assert grep -q 'chown -R "$HOST_UID:$HOST_GID" /home/bun' .devcontainer/Dockerfile]

The `ARG HOST_UID=1000` / `ARG HOST_GID=1000` defaults are preserved and the `COPY .devcontainer/claude-config.json /home/bun/.claude.json` line still appears BEFORE the `ARG HOST_UID` directive (CAM-179 bake-order invariant). [oracle: bun test test/supervisor/claude-config-bake.test.ts]

A new deterministic test reads the Dockerfile text (no Docker daemon) and asserts the new getent branch is present, the group-rename is absent, and the trailing chown is preserved. [oracle: named-command bun test test/supervisor]
Full quality spine is green (typecheck + biome + tests + ratchets). [oracle: bun run check:all]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
userStories.notes: SINGLE-FILE FIX + regression test. Edit only the re-home RUN block in `.devcontainer/Dockerfile` (currently lines ~52-64) and add a new deterministic test under `test/supervisor/` (e.g. rehome-gid-collision.test.ts) mirroring the file-assert conventions in `test/supervisor/claude-config-bake.test.ts` (readFileSync the Dockerfile, string-contains / regex asserts). Target block shape: `RUN if getent group "$HOST_GID" >/dev/null 2>&1; then usermod -u "$HOST_UID" -g "$HOST_GID" bun; else groupmod -g "$HOST_GID" bun && usermod -u "$HOST_UID" bun; fi && chown -R "$HOST_UID:$HOST_GID" /home/bun`. WHY: `groupmod -n` renames a group's NAME but never frees its GID, so the old `groupmod -g $HOST_GID bun` failed with 'GID 20 already exists'; group NAME is irrelevant because chown uses the numeric HOST_UID:HOST_GID. GOTCHAS: (1) `usermod -g <gid>` requires the group to already exist (confirmed against usermod(8): 'The group must exist.'), which is exactly why the getent branch is mandatory, do NOT call `usermod -g $HOST_GID` unconditionally. (2) Do NOT move the CAM-179 `COPY ... /home/bun/.claude.json` line, it must stay BEFORE `ARG HOST_UID` so the trailing `chown -R /home/bun` re-owns it; claude-config-bake.test.ts AC3 guards this. (3) `.devcontainer/` is NOT embedded/vendored, so NO embed-vendor step is needed. (4) CI (macos-latest) has no Docker daemon, so the test can only assert Dockerfile TEXT; a real `docker build --build-arg HOST_UID=501 --build-arg HOST_GID=20` on this macOS host is a SEPARATE operator ceremony hand-filed after the PRD (folds into the combined CAM-178/183 + CAM-179 + CAM-180 rebuild+verify), it is NOT part of this autonomous story. OUT OF SCOPE: HOST_UID user collision handling (documented risk, not a fix); no change to `src/supervisor/worker-container.ts` (resolveHostIds already threads id -u/id -g correctly). Read scripts/cam/patterns.md before coding (Bun runtime, noUncheckedIndexedAccess, test conventions).
